transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-10-14 15:00 PDT | Duration 38m | Recording: on
Attendees: Claire O'Neill (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (CSM); Alex Moreno (Nebula VP Eng), Priya Rao (SRE), Jordan Lee (Data Science), Samir Das (Security), Taylor Kim (Procurement)

[00:00] Claire: Alright everyone, thanks for joining. Quick check — is this still the 38 minute slot? we can take an extra 5 if needed.
[00:28] Alex: Yep fine from us. We're mostly looking to confirm access handoff and get those benchmark runs started.
[01:05] Ravi: Great. Quick agenda: creds and ssh, vpc peering, initial sanity runs (we ran a small batch this morning), KMS/encryption questions, then next steps.
[01:40] Priya: On our side we gave you the temporary IAM role and a service account last night. We want to validate key rotation and restrict the role to the Nebula s3 bucket only.
[02:12] Ravi: Got it. We tested the temporary role — saw 403 on the first attempt but that was because the s3 bucket policy needed the Principal ARN. After we update the policy it should be smooth, that explains the error in the sanity csv.
[03:00] Jordan: Small note — the sample tasks we uploaded are slightly heavier on sequence length than what we'd run in prod, that's intentional to stress the cache.
[03:35] Claire: Thanks, Jordan. On the VPC peering front, Priya, can you confirm the CIDR and whether you allow egress to our managed nat gateway?
[04:10] Priya: We'd prefer no outbound internet for the dedicated pilot; we can do VPC peering and a private link to Redwood's control plane. We need to know what ports and IPs to allow for the node pool.
[04:55] Ravi: Ports 22 for SSH to bastion, 443 to control plane endpoints, and 10250-10255 for kubelet health checks if you're using k8s nodes. We'll send an explicit allowed list.
[05:30] Samir: On encryption, are we using customer-managed keys (CMK)? audit logs retention? we have SOC2 controls to satisfy.
[06:05] Maya: We support both Redwood-managed keys and customer-managed KMS/HSM. For Private/Dedicated we can integrate with your KMS and provide audit log exports. Retention windows can be configured — default 90 days, extendable.
[06:40] Samir: Would prefer CMK, and we'd like the export to our SIEM. Any bandwidth or perf hit?
[07:05] Ravi: Negligible; envelope encryption is applied per-request and doesn't add significant latency. In our internal perf numbers it's sub 5% at token-heavy loads, but we'll validate on your dataset.
[07:42] Alex: Let's talk about the sanity run results. Jordan, can you summarize what you saw?
[08:05] Jordan: Sure. We ran 300 inference calls on the dev harness against the 7B variant. Median latency ~180ms, p95 ~420ms. Those numbers are with no KV cache warmup and sequence lengths ~1.3x production expectation. We were hoping for lower p95 but the tail is probably from cold KV misses.
[09:00] Ravi: That aligns with expectation. We recommended continuous batching and prefix caching; once the workload warms the KV cache the p95 should drop into the 220-260ms range for your seq distribution. Also quantization variant drops per-token CPU but might increase model variance — want to be careful with quality.
[09:40] Jordan: Understood. Can you run a warmed cache benchmark?
[10:05] Ravi: Yes, we'll schedule a warmed run and a steady-state run. We'll also run a config with smaller batch sizes to validate latency SLOs.
[10:40] Taylor: Procurement wants to confirm payment terms for a 4-week Dedicated pilot and trial costs. Claire, can you outline?
[11:05] Claire: We'll send a pricing snapshot for a 4-week reserved pool and a consumption fallback. There's also a short SOW template. I'll follow up in email with numbers — target to deliver by Friday.
[11:40] Priya: One hiccup: our security team wants the audit logs to show per-request token usage for a week; is that currently in the export?
[12:10] Maya: We can include per-request metadata (token counts, model version) in the audit exports. We'll need to scrub PII by default; we can add a toggle for raw inputs if your controls allow it.
[12:45] Samir: We'll need redaction until legal signs off.
[13:10] Claire: Noted. Back to access — Ravi, you mentioned a bastion. Do you need a public elastic IP for it or can it sit behind the customer's NAT?
[13:40] Ravi: Preferably behind customer NAT with static egress IP so we can whitelist. We need SSH access for install but we can support SSM tunnel as well.
[14:10] Priya: We use ephemeral jumpbox creds. We'll create a user for the Redwood installer and rotate after initial setup.
[14:45] Jordan: Regarding model variants — we're interested in trying a quantized 8-bit run to reduce GPU memory. Any risks?
[15:10] Ravi: 8-bit quantization generally reduces memory and cost, but it can introduce small hallucination regressions for some prompts. We'll keep eval sets and a quality baseline; Redwood Optimize can pick a profile per-route.
[15:45] Alex: Could we do canary routing to a model variant for 10% of traffic?
[16:10] Maya: Yes, canaries and A/B are supported in the console, with automatic fallback to the warm model if latency spikes.
[16:45] Taylor: Procurement question — any required attestations or third-party audits before pilot starts?
[17:10] Claire: We have SOC2 Type II and ISO27001 attachments; for Dedicated we can sign an NDA and provide a security package. I'll send the deck.
[17:45] Samir: Also need clarity around data residency — if we run in your EU region can logs be kept in eu-central only?
[18:20] Maya: Yes, regional retention is configurable. For Dedicated on-prem the data never leaves the VPC unless you opt in.
[18:55] Jordan: Quick follow-up — the sanity csv you sent shows 1.2 tokens per call average but our prod is 3.8, so cost projections looked optimistic. Can we re-run with higher token counts?
[19:30] Ravi: Absolutely. Please upload a representative sample of 1k requests and we'll run a cost/latency profile.
[19:55] Alex: We'll get that to you by Friday.
[20:20] Claire: On the timeline: if we clear the VPC peering and firewall by next week we can kick the 4-week pilot the week after. That gives procurement time to sign off.
[20:50] Priya: One operational ask — health checks and autoscaler thresholds. We'll need a recommended config for k8s HPA and node pools.
[21:20] Ravi: We'll share recommended CPU/memory thresholds and a sample HPA yaml. For GPU nodes we also give a recommended burst policy for ephemeral workloads.
[22:00] Jordan: Any known issues with our GPU type? We're using A10G equivalents on prem.
[22:30] Ravi: A10G is fine; we have optimizations for Ampere and Turing. If you go older arch we may need a fallback image. We'll include kernel tuning knobs in the runbook.
[23:05] Maya: Quick sec — I want to call out a subtlety: KV cache sizes and eviction policies can shift tail latency. We'll propose a profile tuned to your median seq length.
[23:40] Samir: If we do CMK, can we have key usage logs forwarded to our key audit?
[24:05] Maya: Yes, we can push KMS usage logs to a customer-owned logging bucket. We'll include steps in the runbook.
[24:35] Taylor: Are there any hard blockers for signing SOW?
[25:00] Claire: Nothing technical blocking — mostly procurement and legal items on your side. From our side we need the final CIDR, an approval for CMK integration, and the sample dataset to run full benchmarks.
[25:35] Alex: Ok noted.
[26:00] Ravi: We'll kick off a warmed-cache benchmark and a steady-state run. Expect two CSVs and a short writeup within 3 business days after we get the sample dataset and VPC details.
[26:40] Jordan: On the warm run can you also include a quantized vs non-quantized comparison?
[27:05] Ravi: Yes, we'll do baseline, 8-bit quant, and a high-batch low-latency config.
[27:35] Priya: One more infra note — our firewall blocks outbound 25/110/143 by default, ensure control-plane SMTP or older ports aren't required.
[28:05] Ravi: Not needed. Control plane uses TLS only.
[28:30] Maya: I'll follow up with the security package link and the SAML SSO guide for the console.
[28:55] Claire: Great. Let's recap actions then.
[29:20] Claire: Action recap: Redwood - run bench and deliver runbook + pricing. Nebula - provide CIDR, dataset, and confirm CMK. Everyone ok with dates?
[29:50] Alex: Yes.
[30:15] Taylor: Procurement will wait for pricing email and then we'll circulate.
[30:40] Samir: Security will review the package and revert by next Wed.
[31:05] Jordan: We'll upload the 1k sample by Friday.
[31:30] Priya: We'll open a ticket for the firewall change and attach the CIDR.
[31:55] Claire: Perfect. Anything else?
[32:10] Alex: No, thanks all.
[32:30] Ravi: Thanks, we'll follow up with the two CSVs and the runbook.
[33:00] Maya: Sending security pack and SAML steps.
[33:25] Claire: Meeting adjourned.

Note: Some words may be mis-transcribed (e.g., "KF cache" instead of KV cache in one snippet).
notes: Tone: practical and task-focused; multiple owners assigned. No technical blockers, a few security confirmations pending. Customer leaned toward Dedicated but will decide based on cost/run results.
